issues.issue: The covenant forbids material changes to Borrower's Required Procedures "without advance notice to, and consent by, the Lender" but fixes no notice period, and "in any material respect" is left unmeasured. Compare the definition of Borrower's Required Procedures, which requires prior written approval in Lender's sole discretion.

The carve-out permits Fund to "make distributions to holders of Investor Membership Interests for the return of capital to the extent required or permitted by Fund's Governing Documents," handing the measure of the exception to an extrinsic document that the Lender does not control. How large a hole that leaves in the Restricted Payments prohibition cannot be read off the Agreement.

Section 8.9(x) makes a default in "capital obligations to any member or former member in connection with their Investor Membership Interests" an Event of Default, while this section allows those very distributions only when no Default has occurred or would result. The two provisions push in opposite directions once redemptions come under strain.

After two specific prohibitions — transfers of property to an Affiliate (a) and acquisitions of Notes Receivable from an Affiliate (b) — clause (c) sweeps in "any other transaction between such Borrower and any Affiliate," subject only to four soft conditions ("ordinary course," "fair and reasonable terms," "fully disclosed," "no less favorable ... than ... arm's length"). The reach of that general catch-all against the enumerated specifics, and the expanded 10% "Affiliate" test that applies only for this Section, are both open to argument.

The whole section is prefaced "Except for Permitted Dispositions and Permitted Investments," and Permitted Dispositions clause (e) allows any sale of a Note Receivable at 80% of the unpaid balance without limiting the buyer, so property may be moved to an Affiliate through the very carve-out clause (a) purports to prohibit. The prohibition and the carve-out cannot both be given full effect.

Proceeds may be used for "funding of its obligations with respect to any Investor Membership Interests or pursuant to a Permitted Reorganization," a phrase that is undefined and would on its face cover using advances to cash out withdrawing members. What counts as such an "obligation" is the whole question.

Section 7.10 prohibits Restricted Payments, which by definition include distributions and redemption payments on Stock in a Borrower, yet this section authorises the use of Advance proceeds for obligations relating to Investor Membership Interests. The permitted use and the payment prohibition overlap without a stated priority.

Subsection (b) caps the Senior Leverage Ratio — Obligations divided by Tangible Net Worth — at 0.9%, which together with subsection (a)'s $600,000,000 minimum Tangible Net Worth allows only about $5.4 million of Obligations, against the $50,000,000 Maximum Revolver Amount committed by Section 2.1(a). Read literally, drawing the facility breaches the covenant from the outset.

Section 8.9(x) makes an Event of Default out of a default in "its capital obligations to any member or former member in connection with their Investor Membership Interests," a category the Agreement nowhere defines, and clause (z) is a general catch-all for "any other agreement" following two specific ones. Section 8.3 similarly turns on whether "any material portion" of assets "comes into the possession of any third Person."

Clauses (e) and (o) provide that amounts Lender incurs "shall be Lender Group Expenses," a term the Agreement never defines; the defined term is "Lender Expenses." Whether those amounts are recoverable Obligations at all turns on a phrase with no referent.

This section lets Lender, "in its sole discretion and without prior notice," set up reserves against the Borrowing Base or the Maximum Revolver Amount whenever a Borrower fails to pay third-party monies, which contradicts Section 2.1(b)'s express agreement "not to establish any such reserves unless a Triggering Event has occurred and is continuing." Both cannot govern the same reserve.

The indemnity is expressly extended to liabilities "WHICH IN WHOLE OR IN PART ARE CAUSED BY OR ARISE OUT OF ANY NEGLIGENT ACT OR OMISSION OF SUCH INDEMNIFIED PERSON," while the closing proviso excludes liabilities "resulting from the gross negligence or willful misconduct." Where a loss is caused partly by ordinary and partly by gross negligence, the two sentences point in different directions.

New York law is chosen for construction and enforcement, yet Sections 2.13(g) and 2.13(h) frame the Borrowers' waivers entirely in terms of Sections 580a, 580b, 580d and 726 of the California Code of Civil Procedure. Which body of law supplies the antideficiency rules being waived is not resolved.

Actions "shall be tried and litigated only in" New York County courts, but the proviso lets Lender bring any suit seeking enforcement against Collateral "in the courts of any jurisdiction where Lender elects." The clause is exclusive against the Borrowers and permissive for the Lender, and how far the "enforcement against Collateral" carve-out reaches is undefined.

The subsection restricts assignments to "Eligible Transferees" in minimum $5,000,000 amounts, then provides that "the Assignee need not be an Eligible Transferee if such assignment is in connection with any merger, consolidation, sale, transfer, or other disposition of all or any substantial portion of the business or loan portfolio" of the Lender. The exception is broad enough to consume the rule.

"Unless the contrary is compelled by the context, everything contained in each Section applies equally to this entire Agreement" is an instruction of uncertain content, apparently meaning the opposite of the headings-only disclaimer that precedes it. What it directs a reader to do with a section-specific term is genuinely obscure.

The section disclaims construction of "any uncertainty or ambiguity herein ... against Lender or Borrowers," removing contra proferentem, and then directs interpretation "according to the ordinary meaning of the words used so as to accomplish fairly the purposes and intentions of all parties." Whether that displaces the ordinary rule against the drafter is itself a question of construction.

The section directs that in the event of a required withholding "Borrowers shall comply with the penultimate sentence of this Section 16.5," but the penultimate sentence of the section is the gross-up proviso, not a compliance direction. The internal pointer does not land where the sentence assumes.

The integration clause says the Loan Documents "shall not be contradicted or qualified by any other agreement, oral or written, before the date hereof," yet the Agreement's operative content depends on pre-closing extrinsic documents — Borrower's Required Procedures and the "written description provided to Lender by Borrowers prior to the Closing Date" in the Permitted Reorganization definition. Whether those documents are excluded or incorporated is unresolved.

Paragraph 5 repeats the representation already given in paragraph 2 of the same certificate but with a different exception formula — "except as set forth on Schedule 2" rather than the earlier carve-out for matters "permitted by Lender." The certificate makes the same statement twice on inconsistent terms.
